findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify or harden the backlog_grew escalation against concurrent-writer count inflation: explain why a shared count growing under normal concurrent load will not be misread as a proven-growing outage (e.g. compare against the same session's prior push, require growth across N successive same-session failures, or key on time-since-oldest-pending rather than raw count).
evidence: Approach pt 2: 'comparing the current unpushed_count against the unpushed count already recorded in the previous push-pending marker ... Ambiguity resolves to False — growth must be PROVEN'
Offending-messages pt 3: 'the count escalates across ALL concurrent sessions'
Operator ruling: 'a merely non-zero or shared backlog count is NOT an outage signal'
backlog_grew (push_state.py:160-179) returns True whenever int(current) > int(prior_count) for two digit counts, with no attribution to persistent vs concurrent growth
findings.finding: The backlog_grew escalation mechanism compares the prior marker's stored count against a freshly recomputed count, but under the plan's own stated concurrency model (~12 concurrent writers, count 'escalates across ALL concurrent sessions') a competing writer's commits landing between the prior-marker write and the current count read inflate 'current' for a reason unrelated to this session's failure, producing a false WARNING escalation. The stated ambiguity->False guard only covers absent/non-digit counts, not two valid digit counts where growth is caused by concurrent (not persistent) load.
findings.location: Approach pt 2 (backlog_grew) and pt 3 (proven-growing backlog -> WARNING)
scenarios: Two writers lose contention in sequence: writer A records unpushed=3; writer B commits and fails; B's backlog_grew reads prior=3, current=5 (includes A's + B's + others' local commits) and escalates to WARNING though nothing is persistently failing — the exact primes-investigation noise the ticket removes
A burst of normal-load concurrent writers monotonically grows the shared count across successive markers, so a healthy contention storm reads as a 'proven-growing backlog' outage
